newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-June 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-June 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- APPLE DAILY-- A group of mainland dissidents in Hong Kong urged the government and influential figures help them to leave the territory. One dissident said he would burn himself to death in protest against the lack of government help.
-- APPLE DAILY -- The government will spend HK$15 million to start a compaign to immunise young people against measles amid fears a major outbreak is imminent.

-- MING PAO -- Yip Kwo-wah, a special advisor of Hong Kong Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa, said that the power of Chief Secretary Anson Chan might be "adjusted" after the handover because Tung liked to do things himself.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The last government land auction before the handover brought in HK$11.6 billion, although the market's response to the sites was not up to expectations.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- Sources said the Chief Executive's Office had drafted new regulations on permament residency different from present practice, under which illegal immigrants would not be given permanent residence even after living in the territory for more than seven years.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Beijing is busy preparing for celebrations marking Hong Kong's handover. Fireworks and lights will keep people in the capital city awake through the handover night.

-- EXPRESS NEWS-- The number of mainland Chinese immigrant students enrolled into local schools reached 15,000 last semester, the most in 15 years. Most are older than their local schoolmates, while their English level is lower.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The future govennment will drop "independent" from the Independent Commission Against Corruption's title, despite the anti-graft commission's view that the word is essential.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Hong Kong businessmen may be charged with corruption for offences committed outside the territory under a new scheme being considered by the Independent Commission Against Corruption.
